transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
After Ukraine strikes on a bridge connecting Russia to Russian-occupied Crimea,
President Vladimir Putin says he will not negotiate any ceasefires covering energy infrastructure.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports Ukrainians are preparing for retaliations.
Russian drones are targeting Kiev and air raid sirens wailed most of the day.
Explosions and the sound of air defense fire rang out across the city.
NPR recorded the explosions while sheltering inside its bureau.
At least one person was killed and many buildings are damaged, including the Austrian and Dutch embassies.
In a post on social media, Ukraine's foreign minister urges the international community to condemn Russia's "terror" in the boldest terms.
President Trump, meanwhile, was meeting with Vladimir Putin in China, where he greeted him warmly, calling him "my friend."
Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News, Kiev.
AI giant Anthropic debuted on Wall Street today at one point surpassing $2 trillion in value.
That's despite fears that the technology threatens lives and livelihoods.
As NPR's John Ruich reports, it's the first time investors can directly invest in AI on the stock market.
AI is changing the way people do a lot of things, from searching for the Internet to developing new medicines.
And Anthropic's right at the center of it, right, with its clawed AI models.
They are among the most advanced models in the world, and they're popular.
Today, Anthropic became the first publicly traded big AI lab that only does AI.
SpaceX is one of its AI rivals, but it does other things like put satellites into orbit.
So prior to today, if the average person wanted investment exposure to AI, it was less direct.
They had to buy shares in companies that make chips, for instance, or software or satellites.
NPR's John Ruich reporting.
The Trump administration is urging a federal judge to let it close the Kennedy Center in Washington, D.C., for two years.
NPR's Anastasia Tsiolkas reports.
Lawyers representing the Trump administration urged Judge Christopher Cooper to let the arts institution close its main complex for a $257 million renovation.
They argued that the renovation plans have been sufficiently scrutinized by the center's board,
which is chaired by President Trump and is mostly made up of his allies.
In September, Trump renewed his threat to tear the center down if his name is not added to it.
The next marquee event is next month, the annual Kennedy Center Honors, which are now slated to be held at Washington's Capital One Arena.
CBS will air the ceremony on December 27. It will also stream on Paramount+.
Anastasia Tsiolkas, NPR News.
The Cincinnati Zoo says Fiona, the hippo, has died after ingesting a visitor's hat more than a week ago.
The zoo's team of veterinarians and keepers tried to keep the beloved hippo hydrated, feeding her treats and monitoring her around the clock.
Fiona became a global sensation after her premature birth in 2017. This is NPR.
The FCC has granted permission to state prisons to jam the signals of cell phones smuggled to inmates.
The technology is already allowed in federal facilities.
Officials say inmates have used contraband cell phones to run drug rings, coordinate prison riots and even order acts of violence.
In Brazil, crews are erecting a protective barrier around the area where an isolated indigenous group emerged this week asking for food.
NPR's Kerry Conn reports pressures from illegal logging may have caused the group to flee.
In an interview with NPR, Luci Alberto Barre says some 20 individuals from the Awa Group peacefully approached an indigenous village in northern Brazil and were provided potatoes and honey.
Barre heads Brazil's indigenous protection agency, Funai.
We are proceeding with great caution to ensure their survival and guarantee that they choose their own path forward, she says.
Barre says it's been more than 12 years since she can remember an isolated group emerging from the rainforest to make contact.
While it's still unclear what prompted the group to seek help, Barre says the Awa's land has been under great threat from illegal loggers and cattle ranchers.
Kerry Conn, NPR News, Rio de Janeiro.
A vibrant landscape painted by Vincent van Gogh weeks before his death has sold for $190.4 million at auction.
The sale of Chateaune on Fleur took place after an agreement between its current owners and a Jewish family that sold it in Nazi-era Germany.
I'm Rylan Barton. This is NPR News from Washington.
This is free through Amazon Music.
Or you can also support NPR's vital journalism and get NPR+ at plus.npr.org.
That's plus.npr.org.
